title: Facilitators may fix Active Data unilaterally only where the error is obvious, unambiguous and indisputable
content:
A.1.13.1.3.1.1 grants a narrow unilateral power: "To correct a clear error, the Core Facilitator may directly update an Active Data document at any time," and "should notify the respective Responsible Party" beforehand. The boundary is stated in the same breath: "if the error or issue is not clearly evident, the Active Data document must be updated in accordance with the established procedure defined in [Direct Edit]."

The Action Tenet at A.1.13.1.3.1.1.0.4.1 supplies the test, and it is deliberately demanding: the mistake must be "obvious, unambiguous, and indisputable," meaning "the mistake is apparent and does not require extensive debate or investigation to be recognized as such."

That definition is the entire safeguard, because it makes the power self-limiting through its trigger rather than through review. Any dispute about whether something is an error is itself proof that the clear-error route does not apply — the standard fails the moment it is contested. A Facilitator cannot argue their way into using it.

Note also that notification is "should," not "must," and it is prior notification rather than consent. Sky accepts a fast unilateral fix for typos and stale references without requiring the Responsible Party's sign-off, on the reasoning that a genuinely indisputable correction has no losing side to protect.
description: The clear-error power bypasses the Responsible Party entirely; anything requiring debate or investigation falls back to the normal Direct Edit process.
